commit.message:
Fix off-by-one in `csp_rtable_set()`

We should consider actually returning an error.
Instead we still just override the last available route,
which seems to have been the previous intention.

Co-authored-by: edvard <edvard@space-inventor.com>

issues.title: build: differences in cmake, meson and waf
issues.body:
It seems like there are some differences in building `csp_rtable_cidr.c` and `csp_rtable_stdio.c`. 
In CMake and Waf everything looks identical, but Meson's build is slightly different:

In `src/meson.build`:
```
if get_option('have_stdio') and get_option('use_rtable')
	csp_sources += files('csp_rtable_stdio.c')
endif

if get_option('use_rtable')
	csp_sources += files('csp_rtable_cidr.c')
endif
```

In `src/CMakeLists.txt`:
```
target_sources(csp PRIVATE
  ...
  csp_rtable_cidr.c
  ...
)
...
if (CSP_HAVE_STDIO)
  target_sources(csp PRIVATE csp_rtable_stdio.c)
endif()
```

In `wscript`:
```
    ctx.env.append_unique('FILES_CSP', [...,
                                        'src/csp_rtable_cidr.c'])

    # Add if stdio
    if ctx.check(header_name="stdio.h", mandatory=False):
        ctx.define('CSP_HAVE_STDIO', True)
        ctx.env.append_unique('FILES_CSP', ['src/csp_rtable_stdio.c'])
```

issues.title: Remove queue and semaphore
issues.body:
Okay here is a biggie, but hear me out.

I believe it is possible to get rid of mutex, by using atomics. Generally this has been easy to figure out. And it saves a Lot of system call work, and works with hardware instructions on most modern platforms. 
(We do still use it one more place which is on the uart driver i believe. )

As for semaphore, we have one use in zmqhub where it's used as a tread guard, because libzmq isn't threadsafe. Here multiple threads are contesting one object. Which is a nice case for a mutex actually. However since zmqhub is Linux only, I feel like this should be solved better somehow. Maybe a Linux specific method.


The final place where semaphore is used in rdp to take the tx task when more work needs to be done. For this where only one task is to be woken. We should be able to do it with a simple wake callback on the conn object. Similarly we need a sleep callback I'm order to suspend the tx task. This is simple and avoids a lot. And of the user wants he can simply ignore sleeping and waking and use polling instead.

I believe we can use something similar instead of the RX queue object for the router task to wait on. By replacing the synchronization of the router task and the input foto, with the aforementioned sleep and wake callbacks we can pretty much get rid of queues too. 

Of course CSP would still rely on queueing. But it's not os dependant any longer. And can be made using simple ringbuffers. 

This is a lot to take on. But i believe it would work. So CSP could actually operate completely without an OS. Neat huh.

issues.title: csp_conn atomics (LR/SC + AMO) raise access faults on targets without atomic support in the backing memory (e.g. TCM/scratchpad RAM); silent hang on first csp_connect()
issues.body:
## Description

`csp_conn.c` uses C11 atomics for connection slot management:
`atomic_compare_exchange_strong()` in `csp_conn_allocate()` and
seq-cst stores to the `atomic_int` fields (`state`, `type`) declared in
`csp_conn.h`.

On RV64 (GCC), these compile to `lr.w`/`sc.w` and `amoswap.w`
respectively. These instructions require the memory system to support
reservations/AMOs, which on SiFive-derived cores (e.g. the U54 in
Microchip PolarFire SoC) is only available for cacheable regions. When
`arr_conn` is linked into a non-cacheable scratchpad region (PolarFire
L2-LIM, and generally any TCM-class RAM), the first `lr.w` raises a
precise access fault -- a synchronous exception -- with a single caller
and zero contention.

Because the fault is synchronous and occurs inside CSP with no error
path, the practical symptom is a silent hard hang of the node on the
first `csp_connect()` (the RTOS trap handler re-enters forever). No
CSP error is observable.

This is a class problem, not board-specific: any deployment placing
CSP state in TCM/scratchpad on cores where atomics require cacheable
memory is affected. Additionally, ARMv6-M cores (Cortex-M0/M0+) have
no CAS hardware at all, so `atomic_compare_exchange_strong` cannot be
implemented natively there either.

Question/proposal: would you accept a PR that guards the slot claim
and state/type updates with the arch layer's critical-section
primitive (interrupt-disable on single-core targets) instead of C11
atomics, or makes the mechanism selectable per platform? The protected
region is a load, a compare and a store. We are running such a patch
locally on RV64/FreeRTOS and Cortex-M0+ nodes.

This patch was suggested by AI, we would also like a fix that would 
work around this without having to change the official CSP files 

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build libcsp v2.1 for a FreeRTOS target where `arr_conn` links into
   RAM without LR/SC/AMO support. Concrete case: PolarFire SoC Icicle
   Kit, all sections in L2-LIM (`> l2lim` in the linker script),
   `CSP_FREERTOS=1`, GCC 8.3 `riscv64-unknown-elf`, `-march=rv64gc`.
2. Initialise CSP (`csp_init()`, register an interface, bind the
   service handler, start `csp_route_work()` in a task).
3. Call `csp_ping(<own address>, 1000, 10, CSP_O_CRC32)` (any
   `csp_connect()` path reproduces it).

Minimal application snippet:

```c
csp_init();
xSelfIface.name    = "SELF";
xSelfIface.addr    = 1;
xSelfIface.netmask = csp_id_get_host_bits();
xSelfIface.nexthop = self_tx;                  /* csp_qfifo_write(p, i, NULL) */
csp_iflist_add(&xSelfIface);
csp_bind_callback(csp_service_handler, CSP_ANY);
/* router task runs csp_route_work() in a loop */
int ms = csp_ping(1, 1000, 10, CSP_O_CRC32);   /* never returns */
```

## Expected behavior

`csp_connect()` allocates a connection; `csp_ping()` returns the
round-trip time (loopback), or at worst an error code.

## Actual Behavior

The hart takes a store/AMO or load access fault inside
`csp_conn_allocate()` and parks in the FreeRTOS trap handler
(exceptions re-enter via mret to the same instruction). The node hangs
silently; no CSP error path is reached.

Debugger evidence: PC parked at the FreeRTOS
`application_exception_handler` (portASM.S); task stack still contains
the 0xA5 fill pattern (fault occurs on the task's first real call).
mcause = (5 or 7)
mepc = 0x800541c

Disassembly of `csp_conn_allocate()` (GCC 8.3, rv64gc, -O0), showing
the three atomic operations involved:

```
0x800541c:  lr.w.aq      a4, (a2)        ; CAS load  (arr_conn[i].state)
0x8005420:  bne          a4, a3, +0xa
0x8005424:  sc.w.aq      a0, a1, (a2)    ; CAS store
0x8005428:  c.bnez       a0, -0xc
...
0x80054ce:  fence        iorw, ow
0x80054d2:  amoswap.w.aq zero, a4, (a5)  ; seq-cst store to conn->type
```

`arr_conn` resides at 0x080184d0 (PolarFire L2-LIM region,
0x08000000..0x08040000, non-cacheable).

## Environment Details

- Build OS: Windows 10/11, Microchip SoftConsole v2022.2-RISC-V-747
- Target OS: FreeRTOS (FreeRTOS-Kernel bundled in the BSP project),
  bare-metal PolarFire SoC MSS (RV64GC, SiFive U54), hart U54_1
- libcsp commit hash: 0d95f6c1eb2a1d6f9c3939ac348055f9ee1d1e22 (tag v2.1)
- Meson version: not used
- CMake version: 4.4.2 (used only to generate include/csp/autoconfig.h;
  compilation is via the SoftConsole managed build)
- GNU Make version: bundled with SoftConsole (GNU Make 4.x)
- Ninja version: not used

autoconfig.h used:

```c
#define CSP_POSIX 0
#define CSP_ZEPHYR 0
#define CSP_FREERTOS 1
#define CSP_HAVE_STDIO 0
#define CSP_ENABLE_CSP_PRINT 0
#define CSP_PRINT_STDIO 0
#define CSP_REPRODUCIBLE_BUILDS 0
#define CSP_QFIFO_LEN 10
#define CSP_PORT_MAX_BIND 16
#define CSP_CONN_RXQUEUE_LEN 16
#define CSP_CONN_MAX 8
#define CSP_BUFFER_SIZE 256
#define CSP_BUFFER_COUNT 10
#define CSP_RDP_MAX_WINDOW 5
#define CSP_RTABLE_SIZE 10
#define CSP_USE_RDP 0
#define CSP_USE_HMAC 0
#define CSP_USE_PROMISC 0
#define CSP_USE_RTABLE 1
#define CSP_BUFFER_ZERO_CLEAR 1
#define CSP_HAVE_LIBSOCKETCAN 0
#define CSP_HAVE_LIBZMQ 0
#define CSP_FIXUP_V1_ZMQ_LITTLE_ENDIAN 1
```

## Logs or console output from the very beginning to the end

```
==========================================
 PolarFire SoC -- libcsp loopback (U54_1)
==========================================
[boot] Installing FreeRTOS trap handler in mtvec...
[boot] Checking endian shim...
[boot]   endian shim OK
[boot] Initialising CSP...
[boot]   addr=1  buffers=10  mtu=256
[boot] Creating kernel objects (static allocation)...
[boot] Starting scheduler -- control passes to FreeRTOS.
[router] ready
[ping] ready
```

(no further output; the first csp_ping() -> csp_connect() ->
csp_conn_allocate() faults and the hart never returns from the
exception path. With the atomics replaced by a FreeRTOS critical
section locally, the same binary runs the loopback ping indefinitely
with stable buffer accounting.)

## Additional Context

- The same statically-linked image, with only `csp_conn` changed to
  use `taskENTER_CRITICAL()/taskEXIT_CRITICAL()` around the slot claim
  and plain `int` state/type fields, runs correctly on the same
  hardware (loopback ping, 5+ minutes, no buffer leak). This isolates
  the failure to the atomics.
- Note that patching only the CAS is insufficient: the seq-cst store
  to `conn->type` compiles to `amoswap.w`, which faults identically,
  so the `atomic_int` declarations in `csp_conn.h` are part of the
  same issue.
- The fault mode is particularly unfriendly because it is invisible:
  no return code, no debug counter, no hook -- the node simply stops.

## Checklist

- [x] I've used GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) to format my text.
- [x] I've avoided using screenshots for console output or logs

issues.title: Multi-Interface, Single-Device Configuration (CSP 1.x)
issues.body:
I'm looking at writing an application that can communicate with the same device over both CAN and UART. I've seen a few mentione ([#342](https://github.com/libcsp/libcsp/issues/342#issuecomment-1020883684), [#331](https://github.com/libcsp/libcsp/issues/331)) of CSP 2.x supporting sending a single message to multiple interfaces for the sake of redundancy.

We were hoping to implement something similar but the device we're using only supports CSP 1.x. The device in question is connected to the main processor via both CAN and UART. We were hoping to implement a fail-safe where the main processor could switch between the two interfaces in the event that the main interface fails.

Is there a standard / recommended way to accomplish this in CSP 1.x? I don't necessarily need both to be active at the same time (and I'm not sure if it even has de-duplication enabled), so would the best option to use `csp_rtable_set()` to switch as needed? I'm not sure if this would introduce a race condition or otherwise cause issues by modifying the routing table at run time (after calling `csp_route_start_task()`.

issues.title: Via Routing doesn't work on CAN with CSP2.0 without promiscuous mode
issues.body:
## Description

During some recent testing I have observed that the Via address specified in a route wasn't used when the packet was routed over the CAN bus, instead the original destination address was used. I am using CSP version 2. To overcome this, I had to make all of the CAN nodes in the network use promiscuos mode. This has consequences for the amount of processing that each node has to do as the packets aren't filtered based upon thier address.

## Steps to Reproduce

The cause is clear from looking at [csp_can2_tx in csp_if_can.c](https://github.com/libcsp/libcsp/blob/develop/src/interfaces/csp_if_can.c), the via argument is ignored, and not used to set the ID in the CAN frame.

```
static int csp_can2_tx(csp_iface_t * iface, uint16_t via, csp_packet_t * packet, int from_me) {
	/* Avoid compiler warnings about unused parameter */
	(void)via;
	(void)from_me;
```

Can you explain the rational behind this?

## Expected behavior

The Via address is used.

## Actual Behavior

The Via address isn't used.

## Environment Details

Provide information about your environment, including:

- Build OS:  Ubuntu 20.04
- Target OS:  Buildroot generated Linux, ARM CPU
- libcsp commit hash: 63e1b05933cccdad5571bc51031c2e8c43b3987b
- CMake version: 3.29.1

issues.title: Split horizon protection prevents packet forwarding
issues.body:
## Description

I am using CSP protocol version 1.

My network setup is a chain of 4 nodes that are interconnected using KISS interfaces:

**Node A**
OS: Linux
Interfaces: LOOP, KISS
Routing table: 12/5 LOOP, 13/5 KISS, 14/4 KISS

**Node B**
OS: Zephyr
Interfaces: LOOP, KISS_A, KISS_C
Routing table: 13/5 LOOP, 12/5 KISS_A, 14/4 KISS_C

**Node C**
OS: Zephyr
Interfaces: LOOP, KISS_B, KISS_D
Routing table: 15/5 LOOP, 12/4 KISS_B, 14/5 KISS_D

**Node D**
OS: Linux
Interfaces: LOOP, KISS
Routing table: 14/5 LOOP, 15/5 KISS, 12/4 KISS

## Steps to Reproduce

Send a packet (e.g. ping) from A to C or from A to D.

## Expected behavior

The packet arrives at C (or D respectively).

## Actual Behavior

The packet arrives at B but is not forwarded. I have traced it down to the `csp_iflist_is_within_subnet()` which filters the packet.

I think I get the concept of the split horizon protection that kicks in here. But is what I am trying to do not reasonable? Am I doing it wrong?

## Environment Details

Provide information about your environment, including:

- Build OS: Debian 12
- Target OS: Zephyr
- libcsp commit hash: e6555c5

issues.title: thoughts on csp_print()
issues.body:
`csp_print()` is a macro but `csp_print_func()` is a function.  `csp_print()` doesn't pass any file related information to `csp_print_func()`. 
 That means that we can't get any file related info, such as `__LINE__` or `__file__` in `csp_print_func()`.

There is no way to replace `csp_print()`.

Also, some OS can print without stdio.  ie) having simple UART driver without full `stdio.h`.  But currently we are either
- having `stdio.h` and `csp_print_func()`, which uses `stdio.h`, or
- `csp_print()` become noop.  no print.

We need third option.  Enable `csp_print()` without `stdio.h`.

To combine the two, I propose: Make csp_print() replaceable so that custom csp_print() can take context info if needed.

issues.title: Increase MTU on packets and add fragmentation on layer 3
issues.body:
Original idea: Implement full support for data buffering and fragmentation. (TCP-a-like)

Proposed change: Increase MTU and provide automatic fragmentation on layer 3. (unless the DF flag is set). This leads to two new fields in the routing table. These fields may be set statically in the table compile time, or discovered by a traceroute.

1) Max MTU
2) Estimated round trip time.

issues.title: Security: unchecked ZMQ frame length can overflow CSP packet buffers; CMP memory services increase impact
issues.body:
## Description

I found security issues in the stock ZMQ path that appear to affect the unmodified example deployment:

```sh
examples/zmqproxy
examples/csp_server -z 127.0.0.1 -a 1 -v 2
```

The primary issue is an unchecked copy in `src/interfaces/csp_if_zmqhub.c`. The receive task allocates/initializes a ZMQ message with a packet-sized hint, but `zmq_msg_recv()` can still receive a larger message. The code then copies `zmq_msg_size()` bytes into the CSP packet frame without checking that the received frame fits in the destination packet buffer.

Affected code path, tested at commit `4352143edba2af45afeb32d5b62ea5746b93a26a`:

```c
/* src/interfaces/csp_if_zmqhub.c */
ret = zmq_msg_init_size(&msg, sizeof(packet->data) + HEADER_SIZE);
...
if (zmq_msg_recv(&msg, drv->subscriber, 0) < 0) {
    ...
}

size_t datalen = zmq_msg_size(&msg);
...
packet = csp_buffer_get(0);
...
memcpy(packet->frame_begin, rx_data, datalen);
packet->frame_length = datalen;
```

This should be treated as a security issue, not only a crash bug. In the stock POSIX/ZMQ example configuration, I was able to validate unauthenticated network-triggered code execution by chaining this packet overflow with reachable CSP management functionality. We have an end-to-end RCE reproducer against the unmodified stock ZMQ example deployment.

We also have several related exploit variants demonstrating different RCE paths and primitives, including memory disclosure, controlled write/callback installation, and full command execution. I am intentionally not attaching those reproducers publicly, but I can share them privately with maintainers.

Related hardening issue: `src/csp_service_handler.c` exposes CMP memory operations. On non-AVR builds, v1 CMP PEEK/POKE use process `memcpy` by default, and v2 PEEK/POKE call configurable memory callbacks. Applications that route unauthenticated packets to `csp_service_handler()` should not expose these services to untrusted peers by default.

## Expected behavior

Oversized ZMQ frames should be rejected before copying into CSP packet buffers. Management services that can read/write process memory should require explicit opt-in and authentication/authorization before exposure to network peers.

## Actual behavior

An unauthenticated ZMQ peer can send an oversized frame that is copied past the packet buffer in `csp_zmqhub_task()`. In the stock ZMQ example deployment, this can be exploited beyond denial of service.

## Environment details

- Build OS: Linux
- Target OS: Linux, POSIX libcsp build
- Transport: stock ZMQ example path
- libcsp commit hash: `4352143edba2af45afeb32d5b62ea5746b93a26a`
- Stock target commands:

  ```sh
  examples/zmqproxy
  examples/csp_server -z 127.0.0.1 -a 1 -v 2
  ```

## Suggested fixes

1. In `csp_zmqhub_task()`, reject any post-fixup `datalen` that exceeds the writable packet/frame capacity before calling `memcpy()`.
2. Ensure all error paths close the ZMQ message and free any allocated CSP packet.
3. Harden `examples/zmqproxy.c` so the capture/logging path does not copy arbitrary-size messages into fixed packet buffers and handles multipart messages correctly.
4. Consider disabling CMP PEEK/POKE by default, gating them behind an explicit unsafe/debug build option, or requiring authentication/authorization before `CSP_CMP` memory operations are reachable.
5. Add regression tests for oversized ZMQ frames and unauthenticated CMP memory operations.

## Private details

I have working private reproducers and validation logs, including an end-to-end stock RCE chain. Please reply here or enable GitHub private vulnerability reporting for this repository, and I can share the full report and PoC privately.

## Checklist

- [x] I've searched in "Issues" for similar issues, both open and closed.
- [x] I've used GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) to format my text.
- [x] I've avoided using screenshots for console output or logs.

- [x] I've provided environment information.
- [x] I can provide logs and the private reproducer through a non-public channel.
